title: Why Hire an Interior Designer — DUMSKAYA DESIGN
description: How an interior designer saves budget and time, prevents renovation mistakes and creates a functional space. Advice from DUMSKAYA DESIGN.

parts.html: An interior designer works out how a home or office will be arranged before the renovation starts: where the furniture goes, where the outlets and lights are, what the finishes are made of. Here are seven reasons to leave this to a professional.

A designer knows styles, materials, and color combinations, and knows how materials hold up in everyday use: which countertop stains easily, which parquet can go over underfloor heating. That is why the interior looks current and stays practical years later.

A knowledge of ergonomics helps use the floor area wisely — especially in small apartments, where every meter counts. A designer also knows building codes and safety requirements, so the project complies with them.
The work starts with you: the designer asks in detail about your tastes, habits, and lifestyle and draws up a brief so that all your expectations are taken into account.

This way the interior works for you specifically. For a family with small children, the designer will suggest safe materials and furniture and space for play and toy storage; for people who work from home, a comfortable workspace.
The designer prepares drawings, plans, and specifications — the basis for construction and renovation work. This helps avoid mistakes and misunderstandings at every stage.

A good set includes furniture layout plans, electrical and lighting diagrams, floor and ceiling plans, and specifications for materials and equipment. With these, builders bring the vision to life precisely, and the renovation runs in a more organized and predictable way — which saves time and money.

Designers have reliable suppliers, manufacturers, and tradespeople they have worked with before. A designer knows who offers what quality and lead times, and can tell you where to buy materials and furniture at a better price.
A designer can also tell you where to find rare decor, unusual materials, antique furniture, or one-off designer pieces if the project calls for them.

A designer’s services may seem expensive, but in reality they help you save money: a designer will steer you clear of mistakes, and a poor choice of materials or furniture means extra spending on rework and replacement.
They know where you can save without losing quality and what is worth paying more for, and they help you stay on budget without unnecessary spending.

Solutions are matched to your budget, taste, and goals: the designer offers several layout and concept options and makes changes based on your comments. At our studio, the package includes one full round of revisions to the visualizations, and “Premium” and “Premium+” include up to two.
3D visualizations show the future space before work begins: scale, proportions, colors, and style. Decisions are easier to make, and there is less risk of being disappointed later.

A designer ties together the work of different specialists: architects, builders, engineers, furniture makers. They make sure the outlets line up with the furniture and the lights with the ceiling structure.
Besides the concept and layout, they select materials, furniture, decor, lighting, and textiles, and during the work they check the quality and make sure it follows the design.

blocks.text: A design costs less than redoing work

parts.html: A design project costs money, but mistakes during a renovation cost more: moving an outlet or relaying tiles after the finishing is done means new work and new materials. A design project settles most of these questions before the renovation begins.

A design project at our studio costs €20 to €70/m² depending on the package, and the consultation is free. Come to the DUMSKAYA DESIGN studio in Bratislava. The studio is headed by Irina Dumskaya, who has more than 15 years of experience.
